data.title: Lindblad Expeditions Expands Portfolio with Major Acquisitions
data.description:

The deal brings pioneering luxury Antarctic interior journeys and vintage aircraft-based adventure itineraries into Lindblad’s portfolio, while White Desert and Echo Charlie will continue operating as stand-alone, founder-led brands, and Patrick Woodhead will assume leadership roles and advise Lindblad on strategic innovation.

The company simultaneously raised its full-year 2026 outlook, now guiding for tour revenues of $850–$880 million, net yield per available guest night of 5.5%–6.5% and Adjusted EBITDA of $140–$148 million, signaling management’s confidence that the acquisitions and strong underlying business momentum will enhance growth and returns for stakeholders.

data.description:

Notable intercepts include 135.15 meters at 2.12 g/t AuEq from 21.30 meters in the northern SHZ and up to 163.95 meters at 0.47 g/t AuEq in the southeast, in areas previously modeled as waste within the maiden mineral resource open pit shell.

data.title: BlossomHill updates BH-30643 lung cancer trial results
data.description:
BlossomHill Therapeutics, Inc. ( (BLSM) ) has issued an announcement.

On September 15, 2026, BlossomHill Therapeutics reported updated results from its ongoing Phase 1/2 SOLARA trial of BH-30643 in non-small cell lung cancer patients with secondary EGFR resistance mutations such as C797S. The data were showcased in a mini-oral presentation at the IASLC 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer in Seoul, underscoring the company’s focus on precision therapies for hard-to-treat EGFR-mutant disease.

Among 40 patients with EGFR C797S-positive resistance to prior EGFR inhibitor therapy, with or without concurrent T790M, BH-30643 delivered a 45% objective response rate and 88% disease control rate, with 63% of patients remaining on treatment at a median follow-up of 6.9 months. Safety data from 174 patients treated at expansion doses showed low rates of dose reduction and discontinuation and mainly Grade 1 wild-type EGFR-related adverse events, reinforcing BH-30643’s tolerability.

Promotion

  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Investigators highlighted the lack of approved targeted options for C797S-driven resistance and described the responses and emerging durability seen with BH-30643 as important evidence that the drug can directly address this resistance mechanism in a heavily pretreated, molecularly heterogeneous population. The results, combined with BH-30643’s prior FDA Fast Track designation, provide clinical validation of BlossomHill’s structure-driven design strategy and support plans to launch a global Phase 2 study in EGFR C797S-positive NSCLC in 2027, potentially strengthening the company’s position in next-generation targeted lung cancer therapies.

The SOLARA trial remains open as a global Phase 1/2 study evaluating BH-30643 across multiple EGFR-mutant subgroups, including on-target resistance mutations, targeted therapy-naive patients and combinations with chemotherapy. Continued dose expansion in diverse settings, along with the planned Phase 2, signals a broad development program that could reshape treatment options for patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC and related resistance profiles, with implications for clinicians and investors watching the emerging OMNI-EGFR class.
